mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market, which typically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and economic activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when RSAFS is declining.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances when INDPRO > 102.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it indicates an inflationary environment with accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real rates remain negative.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and economic activity increase.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals a strengthening demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as construction and related industries benefit.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST > 1500.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in GDP (GDPC1) signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when GDPC1 is declining.
